note: v2.1. A relative term is read slot by slot: LEAD-IN (is it a deadline?) + QUANTITY (number and unit, read by two independent readers that must agree) + QUALIFIER (does it change how days are counted?) + ANCHOR (an event the pipeline can date) + COMPLEMENT (is the anchor the notification of THIS act?) + MOOD (conditional / recital). The code extracts the slots (pipeline/termclauses.py); the rules below decide what each slot value means. Any slot that no rule recognises makes the whole clause UNREAD -> the deadline is RECUPERARE. Rules are evaluated in order inside each slot; first match wins. Nothing here is a legal rule: these are reading rules; the legal parameters stay in rules/terms.json [TO CONFIRM with counsel].

A clause that goes on with a negated perfect ('non è stato effettuato alcun pagamento', 'non ha provveduto') or with 'è decorso / scaduto / spirato', 'inutilmente', 'senza esito' recites a term that has already run - typically the term of an earlier act, which this envelope does not date.
